newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-PLAYERS AND PRESIDENT BANNED FOR HITTING REFEREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLAYERS AND PRESIDENT BANNED FOR HITTING REFEREE.

text.p: Romanian soccer's ruling body has banned a club president and five players for hitting a referee in a first division match last weekend.
The incidents occurred during and after Universitatea Craiova's home match against their long-standing and bitter rivals Sportul Studentesc on Saturday.
With the scores locked at 1-1, referee Sorin Vadana awarded a controversial penalty 15 minutes from time to Sportul, who duly scored and went on to win the match 2-1.
The decision prompted outrage among Craiova's players, officials and supporters who all allowed it to spill over into violence.

Five players have been handed suspensions from one to six games for slapping, shoving and pushing Vadana and the reserve referee while club president Eugen Arnautu picked up a year's ban for slapping Vadana at the official dinner after the game.

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) also banned Craiova from playing their next seven games at their home ground because of rioting by local fans who toppled cars and broke shops windows near the stadium.
"These bans decapitated our club and virtually forced it into relegation to the second division," said Craiova's vice-president Marcel Popescu.
The club is to appeal against the sanctions.
Their one consolation is that the FRF also suspended Vadana for making what they considered to be a faulty decision in awarding the penalty in the first place.
